Done, all four parts.

1. STALE BEADS RECONCILED. PKIX-77k9.1 (was P1), PKIX-gphz, PKIX-qws.1/.2/.3 closed as stale -- RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 are all dispatched in pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs. PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1) deliberately left open and flagged not-to-action, since SHA-1 is refused by design.

2. THE DECISION IMPLEMENTED. pkix-path default = ["rustcrypto"] (758ce9f1), published as pkix-path 0.4.2. Named as the umbrella feature so one place says what the full set is. Constrained environments now turn backends OFF -- default-features = false plus whatever a regulator permits -- and that path is tested: --no-default-features alone, and with rsa, rsa+p256, p256+p384, all check.

3. REGULATED ENVIRONMENTS CONFIRMED, not assumed (dd45bada). pkix-chain/tests/regulated_algorithms.rs, four tests. An algorithm a build will not perform arrives as SignatureNotVerified { reason: UnsupportedAlgorithm }, a curve as UnsupportedKey, a bad key as MalformedKey, and a genuinely invalid signature as SignatureInvalid -- so the four stay distinguishable at the pkix_chain::Error boundary, which is what a FIPS operator needs to avoid chasing a non-existent attack.

Two findings from writing that test, both worth keeping:
- The error arrives as PathBuild(NoValidPath { last_error, .. }), not Path(..), because verify_chain treats an unverifiable signature as AIA-recoverable and attempts reassembly first. That is correct: in a cross-signed topology an alternative issuer may sign with an algorithm this build does support.
- Which means the guarantee DEPENDS on NoValidPath.last_error being typed (PKIX-rm8.29 / PKIX-wnnn.5, done earlier the same day). While it was a Display-rendered String, a regulated deployment would have got prose to grep rather than a variant to match. Had those two beads not landed first, this one could not have been satisfied.

4. INCIDENTAL FIXED. pkix-difftest Cargo.toml no longer claims the umbrella is "rsa + p256 + p384 only" or that Ed25519 is unimplemented. baseline-limbo-analysis.md left alone as the historical capture it is.

One regression along the way, caught by CI and fixed in 2a33baf5: the new default broke x86_64-unknown-none via curve25519-dalek SIMD selection. Extended the bare-metal job existing sha2 soft-backend flag rather than relaxing the gate, since that job exists precisely so "a crate that cannot hold the claim fails here rather than in someone firmware build". thumbv7em and riscv64 were unaffected.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2364 tests, workspace feature powerset clean.

STALE BEADS TO RECONCILE
PKIX-77k9.1 (P1), PKIX-gphz (P2) and PKIX-qws.1/.2/.3 all describe RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and ECDSA P-521 as missing. They are implemented. pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs dispatches all three:
  - OID_RSASSA_PSS (verifiers.rs:74, used at :304, :399, :505)
  - OID_ED25519 (:90, used at :537)
  - OID_SECP521R1 (:59, dispatched at :213)
and the rustcrypto umbrella feature is rsa + p256 + p384 + p521 + ed25519 (pkix-path/Cargo.toml:38). PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1) is NOT stale and should not be actioned: SHA-1 is refused by design.

So 77k9.1 is a P1 describing a past state -- the same pattern the 46-P1 review-epic audit kept finding. It should be closed or rewritten to the remaining work below, not worked as filed.

THE DECISION (2026-11-25)
Assume everything in RustCrypto is available everywhere. Callers should not have to opt into ordinary modern algorithms.

That is not what the defaults do today: pkix-path has default = ["rsa", "p256"]. A plain dependency gets RSA and P-256 only -- no P-384, no P-521, no Ed25519, no RSA-PSS. Those arrive only via the rustcrypto feature, which pkix-chain re-exposes as its own rustcrypto feature and pkix-ct enables directly.

Work: make the full RustCrypto set the default in pkix-path, and follow the change up through pkix-chain. Note this ADDS dependencies for every consumer rather than changing API -- a weight decision, not a semver one -- so it wants a deliberate call on whether the slimmer set stays available as an opt-out.

REGULATED ENVIRONMENTS
The mechanism already behaves correctly and should be preserved, not redesigned. An algorithm that is not compiled in returns VerificationError::unsupported_algorithm(), and an unavailable curve returns unsupported_key() (verifiers.rs:205, :214) -- distinct from MalformedKey, so a caller can tell 'this build does not do that' from 'that key is broken'. Nothing panics and nothing silently succeeds.

What to confirm rather than assume: that those errors stay legible at the pkix-chain boundary, so a FIPS deployment that meets a P-521 or Ed25519 certificate gets an error naming the algorithm rather than a bare path failure. Worth a test per excluded algorithm with the corresponding feature off.

pkix-difftest/Cargo.toml:34 and :40 both describe the umbrella as 'rsa + p256 + p384', predating p521 and ed25519 joining it. {"notes":"CORRECTION 2026-11-25, same day: the SHA-1 aside in this bead closure was wrong.

It said PKIX-qws.4 "must not be actioned" because "SHA-1 is refused by design". That was my inference from DefaultVerifier having no SHA-1 backend, not a decision anyone made, and it contradicts the repository own docs -- PKIX README:227 reads "legacy SHA-1 (feature-gated, off by default, for validating old chains)" and :311 lists it as a P1.

Confirmed stance: VERIFY-ONLY, OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT. PKIX-qws.4 is real work and remains open. Nothing signs with SHA-1 and nothing should, so there is no "create" side; the opt-in feature should sit outside the `rustcrypto` umbrella so that umbrella stays "algorithms we recommend".

Everything else in this closure stands -- RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 are implemented and the defaults are fixed. Only the SHA-1 sentence was false."}
